own_scenes.desc: Tras el pico de la influencia de Kraftwerk en el rock (la trilogía berlinesa de Bowie), surgió en Fráncfort otro «techno» o «tekno», atribuido a Talla 2XLC (Andreas Tomalla), que dirigía el sello Zoth Ommog, fundó el «Technoclub» del Dorian Gray y la revista Frontpage, y estaba en Moskwa TV («Tekno Talk», 1985). A diferencia del de Detroit, venía del hi-NRG y el EBM, estilos europeos. A mediados de los noventa Detroit, Fráncfort y Berlín se mezclaban y la polémica sobre el origen de la palabra seguía viva.

refs.q: Unlike Detroit techno, however, this “tekno” was more connected to “hi-NRG” and “electronic body music (EBM)”—styles that were strictly European.
refs.para: Following a huge peak, Kraftwerk’s influence on rock—Bowie’s “Berlin” trilogy of albums—another sound known as “techno,” or sometimes “tekno,” emerged in Frankfurt, largely credited to Talla 2XLC (Andreas Tomalla). “Talla” is a prolific artist who also ran the Zoth Ommog label, founded the “Technoclub” in the Dorian Gray, and kicked off the German techno magazine Frontpage. He was also a member of the group Moskwa TV, who released a single called “Tekno Talk” in 1985. Unlike Detroit techno, however, this “tekno” was more connected to “hi-NRG” and “electronic body music (EBM)”—styles that were strictly European.
